input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Two material gaps against the fallback. First, Section 14 (p0079) conferred no express convenience right and fixed no notice period: it only obliged TrueLink to keep serving until a date derived from "Client's election", so both the right and its length had to be inferred from a wind-down obligation that could run past sixty days (notice on 1 December ran to 31 January). Operation 1 makes it a direct grant with the fallback's own figure — "Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to TrueLink" — while keeping TrueLink's obligation to serve through the notice period and the "subject to Section 4" qualifier. Second, Section 13 (p0078) auto-renews the one-year term but let TrueLink block renewal on only thirty (30) days' notice, a Vendor no-cause exit on fewer than 90 days' notice, which is the playbook's walk-away band and leaves no realistic migration window for hosting, interface and credit-data services; operation 2 requires ninety (90) days from TrueLink while preserving Client's favourable 30-day notice, so TrueLink can still exit only at the end of a term. No early-termination fee, penalty or unamortised charge exists anywhere — fees are charged per monthly invoice under Section 5(a) (p0045) — so the three-month cap is bettered, and Sections 4 (p0043) and 12 (p0070–p0077) contain no TrueLink at-will exit or exit charge. This lands at the fallback; preferred is not claimed, as we have not sought a flat 30-day notice or a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Clean-up round: correct Section 13's stale "Section 12 herein" cross-reference to Section 14, and fill the blank minimum support period in Section 4 so it cannot be read to fetter the new convenience right.

proposal.summary: Give Client an express right to terminate for convenience on sixty (60) days' written notice, and require 90 days' notice for TrueLink's end-of-term non-renewal.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made Section 14 a direct Client right to terminate for convenience, without cause, on sixty (60) days' prior written notice, replacing the open-ended month-end mechanic with a fixed period so the exit date is certain, and we require TrueLink to give ninety (90) days' notice if it will not renew so its only no-cause exit stays at the end of a term. Our 30-day non-renewal notice is unchanged.

ops.oldText: Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
ops.newText: Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to TrueLink, and, subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the effective date of such termination.

ops.oldText: unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year
ops.newText: unless Client delivers to TrueLink written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days, or TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days, prior to the end of said year
